tonies is the world’s leading interactive audio platform for children, with over 12 million Tonieboxes and 173 million Tonies sold globally. Our intuitive, screen-free system empowers children to learn and play independently in a safe and engaging way.

With a presence in over 100 countries and a diverse portfolio of ~1,500 Tonies across multiple languages, we continue to redefine how children experience storytelling and learning. Since our IPO in 2021, our global team of 630+ colleagues is united by a shared mission: shaping the future of play, learning, and imagination.

Team Lead Functional Analyst (all genders)

Your Role & Impact

We are seeking a strategic, people-focused Team Lead Functional Analyst to head our Functional Analysis & Process Design chapter within the Enterprise Applications & Integrations department. As tonies undergoes a company-wide transformation from a distributed landscape to a harmonized, global operating model powered by SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud, our IT and business functions are moving toward a product-oriented organization.

In this pivotal role, you will provide horizontal leadership to our team of Functional Analysts -the vital translation bridge between our business value streams (Operations, Finance, Sales) and our technical delivery teams. The ideal candidate combines a deep understanding of end-to-end business processes with a strong mentoring mindset, setting methodology standards and empowering the team to translate operational needs into scalable, standard-first enterprise solutions.

What you'll do

As Team Lead Functional Analyst, you will act as the Chapter Lead for Functional Analysis, providing both disciplinary leadership and methodological governance for your team.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Team Leadership & Development: Providing horizontal leadership to the Functional Analyst team, overseeing personal skill development, coaching, and managing capacity allocation across various value streams.

  • Methodology & Standards: Setting and enforcing best-practice methodology standards for the chapter, including process modeling (BPMN 2.0), agile requirements engineering, user story writing (Jira/Confluence), and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) protocols.

  • Strategic Governance: Empowering your team to act as "The Bridge" that effectively translates business pain points into structured functional specification documents (FSDs) while strictly enforcing Fit-to-Standard and Clean Core principles to prevent unnecessary custom complexity.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partnering seamlessly with Business Product Owners (who prioritize the "WHAT & WHY"), SAP Consultants (The Solution), Solution Architects (The Gatekeepers), and App Engineers (The Build) to ensure a unified end-to-end delivery lifecycle.

  • Process Integrity: Ensuring your team upholds strict Segregation of Duties (SoD) guidelines and four-pillar controls during process design (e.g., keeping functional analysis strictly separated from system configuration, master data creation, and security mapping).

  • Transformation Stewardship: Driving the organizational shift from reactive project delivery toward proactive product ownership, helping the business eliminate shadow processes and friction points across boundaries like Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, and Record-to-Report.

What You Bring

You combine a deep understanding of process modeling and enterprise platforms with a consultative leadership mindset, and you enjoy empowering teams in complex transformation initiatives.

You bring:

  • Several years of experience in functional analysis, business process design, or requirements engineering within modern enterprise suites (e.g., SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Salesforce, Microsoft Business Central).

  • Proven experience in a leadership or chapter lead role, with a strong passion for mentoring, team development, and resource management.

  • Deep methodological expertise in BPMN 2.0, Design Thinking, process decomposition, and defining end-to-end test scenarios.

  • Advanced tooling proficiency in Jira, Confluence, Signavio/Lucidchart/Miro, and UAT management platforms.

Release Governance

Who we’re looking for

jobs.title: Product Designer (m/f/x)
jobs.description:
UP42 was founded in 2019 with a clear purpose: to transform how organizations order, access, and analyze Earth observation data. Our platform brings together the world’s leading geospatial providers, and offers a single touchpoint to access, manage, and process data at scale. From vegetation management and infrastructure monitoring to disaster response, UP42 helps organizations across industries find solutions to complex problems through Earth observation. Our expert support team and detailed documentation guide our users through every step. Since July 2025, UP42 has been a part of Neo Space Group.

We are looking for a Product Designer (m/f/x) to join our Design Team in Berlin. You will be the design partner for one of our product teams, working alongside a Product Manager and engineers to take work from an early idea through to something people use. You will own your projects, hold a high quality bar on complex, data-rich interfaces, and work inside a design system you help keep healthy.
You will enjoy this role if you want real ownership of a product area without carrying a whole platform, and if you like going deep into a genuinely complex domain. Our team is complementary, so your work is visible and the feedback loop is short.

What you will do:

  • Take design work from an early idea through to delivery, proposing solutions to blockers rather than only reporting them.

  • Be the reliable design partner for your product team: the person your PM and engineers come to first.

  • Design for complexity: dense data tables, long-running processes, and workflows where the edge cases matter as much as the main path.

  • Look for evidence before you design: talk to users, read what support and sales already know, look at how the product is actually used, and run tests on your own work.

  • Push to understand the problem before designing a solution, and say so when a brief arrives already shaped as one.

  • Scope your own features, break them into pieces, be roughly right about how long they will take, and flag delays early with a plan B rather than a warning.

  • Contribute to our design system, as everyone on our team does: propose and build components, not only use them.

  • Share your work cross-functionally, take feedback, and iterate; notice improvements inside your area and act on them, instead of waiting to be asked.


Here is a good summary of what we are looking for:

  • Experience delivering product design work end-to-end inside a cross-functional team.

  • Solid interaction (IxD) and visual/UI design skills, with the ability to make complex data and workflows understandable.

  • Strong Figma skills, and a working understanding of how a design system is actually built: how a component is structured, how it behaves, and the rules it has to respect. You will be a contributor to ours, not only a user of it.

  • Experience using research and product evidence to make design decisions: usability tests, customer conversations, support tickets, product data. We are not looking for one particular method.

  • Comfortable telling the difference between what we know and what we are assuming, and willing to say which is which.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity: able to make progress when the picture is still incomplete, and to adjust when what you learn changes the direction.

  • Able to scope your own work and communicate honestly about time, collaborative, feedback-driven, and proactive about the problems you can see.

  • Fluent in English and based in Berlin with hybrid work capability.

Bonus points if you bring:

  • Experience designing geospatial, enterprise, or data-heavy B2B products.

  • Background in UX research, data visualization, or complex workflow design.

  • Knowledge of accessibility and inclusive design.

  • Experience with interactive prototyping.

  • Awareness of current AI tools and emerging opportunities in UX processes, with an understanding of how AI can enhance user outcomes without adding unnecessary complexity.

Let us tell you why UP42 is a good choice:

  • Let’s disrupt the industry: You get the chance to shape the state-of-the-art geospatial processing platform and create a completely new planetary perspective

  • Let’s stay flexible: We practice a hybrid working model - you can choose when to work from the comfort of your home or join your colleagues in our modern office in the heart of Kreuzberg, or even from a global place of your choice up to 90 days per year

  • Let’s win as a team: We’re an inspiring international team working in a fun and productive environment

  • Let’s be fair: We offer a competitive salary package and other perks such as wellbeing initiatives, sponsored fitness subscriptions, an educational budget for your personal development and public transportation discount - just to name a few

  • Let’s enjoy the good side of life: Gather in regular team events as well as our global company parties twice a year

  • Let’s think outside of the box: There are challenges and enough space for creativity and taking ownership

Does this sound like a good next step into your geospatial career? If so, we look forward to receiving your application in English.

Our culture is one of belonging, where everyone feels welcome and where differences are celebrated. We seek to recruit the best talent regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background and/or belief—and strongly encourage people from underrepresented groups to apply. We also value more than the skills and experiences outlined in this job description. Even if you think you only fill 60% of the requirements for this role - we would still like to consider your application.

What you'll own as our Senior AI Product Designer

Your mission is to bring consumer-grade craft to a B2B healthcare product used by clinicians and hospital administrators under real time pressure, and to help invent the design patterns for AI-native surfaces that don't exist anywhere else yet.

  • You design the AI-native surfaces our platform is built around, including multi-modal interfaces, agent state, uncertainty, and human-in-the-loop controls, inventing the patterns as you go rather than adapting existing ones.

At Oxa, we're building the future of Industrial Mobile Autonomy (IMA) and are in the market for new talent.

Oxa’s customers are the operators of some of the world's largest industrial facilities. Our technology transforms existing industrial vehicles into intelligent autonomous fleets, unlocking new levels of productivity, safety, and performance.

 

‘The phone in your hand, the coffee on your desk, the shirt on your back - they all moved through a web of ports (air and sea), distribution yards and manufacturing hubs. This is the invisible circulatory system of global trade, and it relies entirely on a relentless, repetitive shuffle of goods. Towing.

This towing task happens in complex, commerce-critical industrial environments. Here, having self driving technology “do the driving” delivers immediate, measurable impact. IMA will revolutionise the movement of goods across the world's ports, airports, and yards.

You can be part of that as an Oxbot’

‘Paul Newman - Founder and CEO’

 

Our Products:

Our products are built on four core technology pillars which come together to build a complete system:

Oxa Ware – Our modular autonomy hardware systems for consistent and repeatable integration of autonomy with existing vehicles.

Oxa Driver – Our Physical AI, embodied in Oxa Ware, self-driving software that enables vehicles to perceive, reason, and drive autonomously in complex real-world environments.

Oxa Foundry – Our development toolchain that leverages generative AI to continuously train and assure Oxa Driver, synthesising situations and sensor data.

Oxa Hub – Our suite of cloud services for monitoring, managing and orchestrating fleets driven by Oxa Driver, including an API for integration with existing logistics systems.

 

Behind these technologies is our exceptional team, the Oxbots. We are home to some of the world's leading experts in autonomous systems, robotics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, and distributed software engineering. Together, we're solving some of the hardest technical challenges in autonomy, turning the research and development we do into production and deploying it into environments. Making robots do useful work.

 

Your Team:

You will join the Data layer of Oxa Driver: the teams that train, teach and test the machine-learning systems our vehicles rely on. They turn data from our vehicles and simulation into the datasets, scenarios and tools the rest of the stack builds on, and their workload grows with each new operating domain and site we take on.

Data is a group of teams responsible for:

  • collecting and curating real-world data, including dataset quality and labelling

  • generating synthetic sensor data to fill gaps in real-world coverage

  • simulation and digital twins of the sites our vehicles operate in

  • the data infrastructure that stores, organises and serves this data

  • applying machine learning to hard problems across the stack

The teams work closely with Autonomy Applications, who train and deploy models on this data, Integration & Test, our data ingest and platform teams, our safety team, and the Solutions team who take our products to customers.

Your Role:

Our Technical Program Manager is the delivery enabler for the Data teams. They coordinate delivery so the teams can collect, curate, generate and ship data with less friction, and their leads can focus on engineering.

They will work with engineering, product and solutions leaders across the stack who own customer outcomes. The focus of the Program Manager is to make sure the datasets, simulations and tools other teams depend on arrive when planned, with risks and dependencies visible early.

This role will be based in our Oxford office, with occasional visits to our vehicle sites to support understanding of how data is collected and used.

 
 

Your Responsibilities:

  • Take the layer's commitments in our product engineering plan and, with the leads, turn them into sequenced work with dates and a clear definition of done. Bring the teams' planning into Jira in a way that adds little overhead, and keep work traceable to the products it supports.

  • Run the regular triage of data-quality issues that affect model training, such as calibration, timing and labelling problems. Make sure every issue has an owner, a priority and a next step.

  • Coordinate the data, scenarios and simulation each new operating site needs, so they are ready when the site goes live.

  • Run the layer's cloud cost reporting, and help leads balance cost against keeping available the data that teams need.

  • Track what the teams need from others and what others need from them, raise conflicts early and broker the trade-offs:

    • data from our vehicles and ingest pipelines

    • datasets, scenarios and simulation for model training and testing

    • external labelling and cloud compute providers

  • Report monthly progress against plan, plus data-quality and cost health. Use simple metrics, such as dataset turnaround time and cost per training cycle, to show whether delivery is improving.

  • Find the friction, such as manual curation steps, unclear ownership or slow data turnaround, and drive fixes with the teams.

What you need to succeed:

  • A career that started in engineering (a degree in computer science, software, data, electrical, robotics or similar) and have moved into delivery, with 2+ years as a TPM, project engineer or delivery manager on a technical product.

  • Knowledge of the data and ML lifecycle: You know how data moves from collection through curation, labelling and dataset release to model training and evaluation, and why data quality and versioning matter. Hands-on experience in data engineering, machine learning or simulation is preferred but not essential.

  • Data and cloud fluency: Enough to follow the engineering and ask good questions: data pipelines, cloud storage and compute, datasets and labelling, and simulation.

  • You break down work, map dependencies and forecast from data (using tools like Jira, Confluence and Miro), and you build trust with engineers when priorities shift.

Extra kudos if you have:

  • Experience in automotive, robotics or other autonomous systems.

  • Experience with MLOps, data platforms or labelling operations.

  • Exposure to simulation, synthetic data generation or digital twins.

  • Experience tracking or optimising cloud spend.

  • Comfort with Git-based planning, documentation-as-code, or AI tools for reporting.

Your Interview Experience:

Our interview process is designed to give you every chance to get the measure of us, and us of you. You will join three stages which will give you every opportunity to show your strengths and qualities, via scenario based questions and technical exercises.

 

What We Offer:

About Pelico

Traditional industrial manufacturing systems were built for predictability. Supply chains no longer are. Today, real-time data is buried in legacy tools that weren't designed for constant disruption. By the time an issue surfaces, it has already snowballed, sending everyone into firefighting mode. Pelico exists to close the gap between production plans and the daily reality on the factory floor.

We've built the manufacturing orchestration platform trusted by the world's most complex industrial operations : companies like Airbus, Boeing, Safran, Eaton, and Cartier. Our AI connects fragmented supply chain, production, and quality data into a single live operational picture — then puts AI agents to work anticipating disruptions, simulating recovery options, and keeping every team aligned before small problems become expensive ones.

Founded in 2019 and backed by General Catalyst, 83North, and Serena, we've raised $72M and are growing fast — 300% year-over-year revenue growth, deployed in 15+ countries, and supporting factories worldwide. We're headquartered in Paris, with offices in Miami, London and Amsterdam, and we're just getting started.

This is a rare chance to join a company that's redefining an industry that hasn't been disrupted in decades — from the inside.

About the Role

Pelico is hiring a Senior Product Manager — Core Platform to own one or more of the shared components that every Pelico product is built on.

Pelico is moving from features built per use case to a platform of configurable components: the data model and the engines that compute on it, the configuration layer, UI building blocks, workflows and actions, and the platform services around them. Solution teams, forward deployed engineers and AI agents combine these components to deliver a use case for a customer. The quality of that base decides how fast Pelico delivers, how well it scales and whether customers trust what they see.

You will own part of that base and run it as a product. Its users are internal teams and agents as much as planners and buyers at customer sites. The exact scope depends on your profile and the team's needs. The role is technical: you need to discuss data structures, APIs, performance and configuration models as easily as user workflows.

What You'll Do

  • Own one or more platform components end to end. Depending on the team's needs, this can be the data model and how customer data maps into it, the computation engines, the configuration layer, configurable UI building blocks (tables, detail views, dashboards), the action library and write-back to customer systems, or platform services such as access control and notifications.

  • Treat internal teams as your customers. Understand what solution PMs, forward deployed engineers and the agent team need, and turn repeated requests into reusable components instead of one-off builds.

  • Make components configurable, not custom. Decide what is configured, at which level (common, solution, customer), and where custom code is still acceptable. Cut the time it takes to deliver a new use case.

  • Design for agents as well as people. Give components clear interfaces so workflows and AI agents can call them as tools, with audit, limits and approvals.

jobs.title: Engineering Manager
Defense Success Manager, France
jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The Role

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

  • Roughly a fifth of your time is protected, rotating build time for exactly this work; it is part of the job, not extra to it.

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of experience owning outcomes for enterprise or institutional customers of technical products or deployed solutions — adoption and commercial outcomes (retention, renewal, expansion), not relationship management or activity reporting.

  • Strong technical fluency in secure enterprise deployment models. You can identify what a deployment type (on-premise, disconnected, air-gapped) means for available features, telemetry, upgrades and accreditation, and you validate specifics with technical teams instead of assuming parity.

  • Ability to engage credibly with architects, engineers, IT and security stakeholders, while translating technical trade-offs into clear implications for mission owners and executives. You know when to bring in a deeper technical expert.

  • Comfort operating under security, compliance and confidentiality constraints, including restricted or classified environments and strict information-handling rules.

  • Strong ownership and builder energy. You have created structure or improved a process in an ambiguous, fast-moving environment and are motivated to build a company, not wait for clear directions.

  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management and execution skills. You align teams without formal authority, surface risks early and drive decisions through to completion

  • Analytical and commercially minded: you can define meaningful success metrics with imperfect data, assess customer health, and are comfortable carrying renewal and NRR accountability.


Nice to have

  • Experience serving defense, public sector or critical infrastructure customers, including sovereign or classified programs.

  • Experience with AI, machine learning, data platforms or complex enterprise software, including production deployments in regulated or security-sensitive environments.

  • Experience working alongside deployment, engineering or professional services teams on custom use cases, and the transition from implementation to ongoing operation.

  • Familiarity with public procurement, framework agreements and multi-year option structures.

Security & Compliance criteria

  • Eligibility: must hold citizenship in the target territory (France for now).

  • Clearable: must meet all local requirements for high-level security clearance (e.g. no criminal record, fulfillment of national service obligations).

What We Offer

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

Privacy Policy

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

lemlist is moving upmarket. We’re hiring a GTM Experience Manager to build our field marketing channel from scratch: bring in bigger deals and help our strategic customers stay and grow with us.

You’ll decide which conferences are worth investing in, what to build with partners and which events we should run ourselves. You’ll own the budget and make it happen, working closely with Marketing, Partnerships and Sales.

The scope is worldwide, with a focus on Europe and our Paris HQ as the home base for our own events.
It includes events for lemlist but also for claap, the sales intelligence platform we bought one year ago (same target audience).

What your impact will look like

Within 3 months, you’ll have:

  • Drafted our field strategy for lemlist: audience, objectives & how to reach them through events & strong sales/partners collaboration

  • Identify, negotiate & start action plan for 2 must-attend paid Events for lemlist

  • Started creating one owned event format that can become recognizable lemlist franchise (eg. GTM monthly breakfasts…)

Within 12 months, you’ll have:

  • Made lemlist events a must-be place for our ecosystem and audience

  • Run regular workshops for our top customers with CSMs, our Product leaders and/or our CEO, driving measurable adoption and upsell, and producing a steady flow of customer storiesz

  • Become the internal expert on the GTM event ecosystem (paid & partners): you know all the relevant events globally, who attends them, which ones are emerging and which ones are declining

  • Built a clear investment strategy across sponsored events & owned events with a strong point of view on where we spend and why

  • Build strong relationships with our key partners & some GTM communities, thanks to successful events

  • Built a repeatable playbook for selecting and activating the right Sales reps at each event so we maximise impact before, during and after

  • Bonus project: launch the lemlist swag store and build a rewards program to engage prospects, celebrate users and strengthen partner relationships.

What you’ll do concretely

You’ll manage two main types of events:

  • Sponsored events:

    • third-party conferences and trade shows.

    • You’ll build lemlist’s presence through booths, speaking opportunities and creative activations (eg. lemlist @ VivaTech)

    • …sometimes by creating our own event around a major industry moment.

  • lemlist events:

    • experiences organised by lemlist for prospects, customers or both.

    • Meetups at our HQ, the lemhouse in Avignon, executive dinners, IRL workshops in coffees or any venue of your choice.

    • Webinars with our team, partners a/o users, for our prospects & clients

    • You may run them independently or with some of our partners.
      → Recent examples: Event for a client at our HQ ; Hackathon with Clay and HubSpot.

Curate the right events and partners

  • Spot the difference between an outdated tradeshow that won’t attract our buyers anymore and the next place our audience will actually want to be (eg. recent AI / GTM trendy events)

  • For sponsored events, evaluate sponsorship opportunities based on audience quality, pipeline potential and brand impact. Assess audience & sponsor list (competition can be a good sign), ask feedback to operators that have been there.

  • Negotiate sponsorship packages to secure the best value, visibility and booth location. There is ALWAYS room to negotiate.

  • Proactively identify the right partners to build events with, and know when to push back on opportunities that are not worth our time.

Create content people want to show up for

  • Find and convince great speakers to join us for our events. Including customers, sales leaders, operators and partners.

  • Define sharp themes and angles that reflect what our audience genuinely cares about.

  • Oversee the creation of agendas, talks, workshop programs and speaker materials, with support from the wider Marketing team.

Deliver memorable experiences

  • Own every event from idea to execution, ensuring a smooth experience for attendees, speakers, partners and the lemlist team.

  • Manage vendors and logistics, including venues, catering, booth production, room setup, equipment and travel, with support from our Office Manager for in-house events.

  • Design experiences people remember, whether through a creative booth activation, an unexpected format or standout branding.

  • Stay calm when plans change at the last minute. Because they will.

Turn events & content into pipeline

  • Work closely with our French and EMEA Sales teams to define the audience, targets and pipeline objectives for our events.

  • With our sales leads, select and organise (in advance!) the right lemlist reps for each event.

  • Get Sales moving before the event: activating their networks, booking meetings and running targeted outreach.

  • Own the follow-up plan after the event so conversations turn into real opportunities

Own the budget and performance

  • Own a €300K annual budget covering field marketing activities.

  • Track sourced and influenced pipeline, meetings, opportunities and conversion rates, then share clear post-event learnings.

About you

  • B2B SaaS native: you know the European Sales and GTM ecosystem, its key players, communities and events.

  • Passionate about Sales: ideally, you’ve worked in Sales yourself and instinctively know which topics, angles and formats will resonate with our audience.

  • Performance-driven: you can own a budget and prove its impact. You think in meetings, opportunities, pipeline and revenue.

  • Hands-on: you can build a European strategy one day and fix a missing microphone the next. Neither is beneath you.

  • Strong editorial instinct: you understand Sales and know why people show up, what they’ll remember and what they’ll tell others about.

  • Great with people: you know how to get Sales reps, speakers, partners and vendors moving in the same direction.

  • Highly organised: you can run several events at once and stay calm when something inevitably goes wrong.

  • A fierce negotiator: you negotiate hard, spend carefully and never accept the first sponsorship package.

  • Fluent in English (French is a plus)

Bonus points

  • You’ve created an event or activation people were still talking about months later.

How to apply & recruitment process

jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer - XTM One
jobs.description:
🌀 The Company

Founded in 2022, Filigran is a global cybersecurity company on a mission to empower defense teams to be proactive through open-source solutions that uncover threats and drive action.

Filigran stands out in the cybersecurity ecosystem through its open-source, AI-powered and threat-informed approach to Continuous Threat Exposure Management (CTEM). Our eXtended Threat Management (XTM) platform brings together threat intelligence, exposure validation and cyber risk reduction, enabling organizations to better understand their threat landscape and take action.

At the heart of Filigran is our open-source approach. Our vision is to unite defenders into a global community to make security more open, resilient and collaborative.

As Filigran continues to scale globally, we are building the organization, infrastructure and capabilities needed for our next stage of growth. How we scale matters just as much as how fast we scale: our CORE values: Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity shape how we work together, make decisions and build for the future.

 

🎯 The Role

We're looking for a Principal Software Engineer to define and drive the technical direction of XTM One, Filigran's AI platform for threat informed defense and the agentic core of the XTM Suite.

XTM One creates and runs cybersecurity expert AI agents and dispatches their intelligence across OpenCTI, OpenAEV and OpenGRC. It also hosts the suite's shared commons (unified authentication, consolidated datasets, configuration) and ships both as SaaS and on premises. Every XTM product connects to it, which makes its architecture one of the most structuring technical decisions at Filigran.

This is not a management role: no headcount, no sprints. You own the technical craft, standards and vision of XTM One, and you carry them into the XTM Foundation, where the engineering principles shared by all products are set for the 60+ engineers at Filigran.

💼 Your Responsibilities

Vision & architecture

  • Define and carry the technical vision of XTM One over the long term, with technical and product leadership.

  • Own the platform architecture: agent runtime and orchestration, tool and MCP integrations, data and context layers, APIs, permission model, shared commons.

  • Design for SaaS and on premises from day one: multitenancy, isolation, upgrade paths, configuration, operability in customer environments.

  • Arbitrate key decisions on scalability, resilience, security, maintainability and cost, including LLM latency and inference cost.

Standards & quality

  • Define the team's technical principles (architecture patterns, code quality, tooling, CI/CD, testing, development with AI assistants) and get them applied through docs, reviews, pairing and example.

  • Set the bar for observability and reliability of nondeterministic AI workloads: metrics, logs, traces, evaluations, and guardrails that make agent behavior measurable and debuggable in production.

  • Keep the right balance between features, technical debt and innovation.

Integration across products & XTM Foundation

  • Define how OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenGRC and future products integrate with XTM One: contracts, authentication, data exchange, versioning.

  • Be a full member of the XTM Foundation: bring the XTM One perspective in, carry its decisions back, and keep coherence with the other Principal and Staff Engineers.

In the code

  • Write production code, prototype new approaches before the team adopts them, review critical PRs so that feedback teaches, and unblock engineers.

🤝 Who You'll Work With

  • Reports to: VP of Technology

  • Key collaborators: XTM One engineering team and its verticals; XTM Foundation (Principal and Staff Engineers across OpenCTI, OpenAEV, OpenGRC); Product leadership; open source contributors.

  • Working model: embedded in the XTM One team, with regular XTM Foundation work.

🧬 Profile We're Looking For

  • 10+ years in software engineering, with technical leadership on complex production platforms.

  • Strong fullstack background, with a backend and architecture focus. You master TypeScript and Python, the core languages of XTM One, and you can take a feature from the data model all the way to the UI.

  • Strong system design: distributed systems, scalability, performance, security, observability.

  • A 360° view of software engineering: product need, design, code and tests, CI/CD, packaging and release, infrastructure and deployment, production operations, monitoring, incident response. A container image or an upgrade path is as familiar to you as an API contract.

  • Built and operated platforms delivered both as SaaS and on premises, including multitenancy and enterprise constraints.

  • Strong AI affinity. You've been building with LLMs by choice for a year or two, with LLM systems in production: agent frameworks, tool calling, MCP, RAG and vector search, evaluation, and the discipline to make them reliable.

  • Technical watch is part of the job. You keep up with your craft deliberately (reading, experimenting, prototyping) and turn what you learn into concrete proposals.

  • You define and carry technical standards: you raise the bar on a team, you don't just follow it.

  • Excellent written communication in English: design docs, ADRs and review comments that others learn from.

  • Autonomous and at ease in a remote, asynchronous culture; you drive problems to resolution and enable others instead of becoming a bottleneck.

  • Bonus: cybersecurity domain knowledge (CTI, CTEM, MITRE ATT&CK, STIX/TAXII); extensible plugin or tool ecosystems; open source contributions or maintainership.

🛡️ About XTM One

XTM One is Filigran's AI platform for threat informed defense. It is dedicated to creating and running cybersecurity expert AI agents and dispatching their intelligence across the products of the XTM Suite.

Every product of the XTM Suite is connected to XTM One to leverage AI agents for a more proactive platform that is easier to use. Within XTM One, agents can use and correlate data across products to make the most meaningful assessments and take the most relevant actions. XTM One also hosts shared commons such as unified authentication and consolidated datasets and configuration.

🌱 Why Join Filigran? More than just a job.

We are a fast-growing, global and remote-first company, and we believe the best work combines purpose, impact and innovation. You’ll work alongside talented people across the world who care about what they build, how they build it, and the impact they make on the broader cybersecurity ecosystem.

⭐ Be part of something bigger

We believe we do work that matters. Our open-source approach means that work extends beyond Filigran. You’re contributing to technology and ideas that strengthen a global community of defenders and help make cybersecurity more open and collaborative.

💻 Work at the edge of what’s next

We bring together cybersecurity, open source and AI — giving you the opportunity to work with emerging technologies, experiment with new ways of working, and contribute to how they are applied in practice.

🌍 Global opportunity without borders

Be part of a fast-growing, truly international team — collaborating across Europe, North America, APJ and beyond, with the flexibility of a remote-first environment. As we grow, you’ll have opportunities to expand your scope, take ownership, learn quickly and grow with us.

🧭 A culture grounded in CORE

Cohesion, Openness, Responsibility and Equity define how we work together — with openness, ownership, collaboration and respect. These are the principles that guide how we make decisions, treat people and grow together, especially when no one’s watching.

💰 What you can expect

  • Competitive compensation + equity — everyone shares in our success

  • Remote-first flexibility — work from wherever you’re based, with flexibility built into how we operate

  • 25 days PTO baseline — real time to disconnect, recharge and enjoy life outside work

  • Volunteer days — paid time to contribute to causes that matter to you

  • Set up for success — choose the equipment that works for you, with additional support for your remote work and development needs as our programs evolve

  • Two annual in-person get-togethers — one global company get-together and one team get-together, creating dedicated time to connect, collaborate and strengthen our culture beyond the screen

🌍 Equal Employment Opportunity

We enable cybersecurity through inclusion — from code to culture.

At Filigran, we are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We believe the diversity of our people makes our products and our team stronger. We welcome talent of every background, identity and lived experience, regardless of race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability or veteran status.

What matters here is what you bring, not what you look like, where you’re from or how you identify.

🚀 Ready to Join Us?

Apply now and help us build the future of the cybersecurity ecosystem, together.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer - Payments Team
jobs.description:
Join a fast-growing, listed company with a purpose! Fastned owns and operates a network of 400+ fast charging stations across 10 European countries, allowing electric vehicle drivers to charge their car with 100% green energy in just 15 minutes. Our goal is a European network of 1000 fast charging stations in prime locations, where all electric vehicles can charge with renewable energy from the sun and wind. We have recently been voted best charging network in the UK, France and the Netherlands. If you want to make a difference and work in an informal, international scale-up environment with future prospects, then read on!

Your role

Fastned aims to accelerate the transition towards sustainable mobility by giving fast charging to electric drivers. Part of that mission is making car charging as simple as charging your phone, and paying for it should be just as effortless. As a Backend Engineer in the Payments team, you will help make paying for a charge frictionless, secure and reliable. Drivers can pay through the Fastned app, by QR code or with a contactless card at the charger.

The team owns Fastned’s payments domain end to end. That covers integrations with payment service providers and payment terminals. It also covers the services behind payment methods, wallets, pre-authorisation and session payments, billing, invoicing and dunning. The stakes are high: Fastned handles 23,000+ charging sessions a day, and every one of those payments goes through our systems. We’re now moving towards real-time payments, where each session is paid instantly instead of invoiced later. As we are growing and adding roaming features as a Mobility Service Provider, there are many scale relevant challenges to solve.

We have no legacy systems. You’ll work with Kotlin 2.x, Java 21+, and Spring Boot 4 on most services, AWS, Kubernetes, Kafka, SQL (Postgres), Terraform, GitLab CI/CD and REST APIs to build scalable, fault-tolerant services that drivers and our Finance team rely on every day. We encourage responsible AI usage and provide tooling like Claude Code, Codex, Dust. 

You’ll work closely with the other product teams, alongside fellow Backend Engineers, Data, Design, an Engineering Manager and a Product Manager in a Scrum setup. This role suits an engineer who enjoys a complex domain, cares about getting the details right, and wants to grow by taking real ownership of business-critical systems.

Your overall responsibilities include

  • Designing, developing, testing and reviewing reusable, maintainable and scalable code

  • Working AI-first: using AI-augmented engineering, agentic workflows and AI tooling as a natural part of how you design, build, test and review, with judgement for where AI is a multiplier and where humans stay in the loop;

  • Taking ownership from discovery to post-production;

  • Taking operational responsibility for what you build, including monitoring, alerting and incident analysis;

  • Helping improve engineering methodologies and best practices


Who we are looking for

In order to be successful in this role, you bring a strong sense of ownership and a pragmatic, proactive mindset. You enjoy working in a collaborative scale-up environment where things can change quickly and where taking initiative matters.

Additionally, you tick the following boxes:

  • You have 3+ years of professional backend experience, with strong hands-on Kotlin and/or Java experience.

  • You have previous experience in the payments domain.

  • You have experience working in agile teams within an international, multicultural environment.

  • You have experience building and operating microservices in production, using REST APIs, cloud platforms and relational databases.

  • You are familiar with event-driven architectures and technologies such as Kafka.

  • You care about reliability, maintainability and the operational impact of the software you build.

  • You spot opportunities and problems and pick them up yourself instead of waiting for a ticket.

  • You use AI tooling as part of your engineering workflow, with sound engineering judgement.

  • You are fluent in English and have an affinity with Fastned’s mission.

Nice to have

  • Experience in e-mobility, energy, charging infrastructure or another operationally complex domain.

Join us in building a better future

We work hard to change the world, but we don't forget to recognise & celebrate our successes, big and small. We focus on work-life balance, provide genuine work flexibility, and have family-friendly policies in place.

Electric mobility is new territory for you? Don’t worry!

As part of your onboarding, you will participate in a series of exciting workshops where you will learn everything about our industry and fast-charging infrastructure.

Our benefits package includes:

  • Stock option plan - we believe in shared value creation.

  • Pension plan (fully covered by Fastned).

  • A training and development budget of €3,000 per year per employee, because development and training are important to us and our sector offers endless opportunities.

  • In order to experience and enjoy the EV life, you get access to our fully electric vehicle fleet (all charging expenses covered), which is also for private use.

  • 29 holidays. Additionally, we give you two mission days you can use to contribute to Fastned’s mission or to support a cause that is important to you.

  • Going the extra mile for parents: We provide you with personalised coaching support before, during, and after parental leave, facilitated by Foundree.

  • Understanding women's health is beneficial for all of us, fostering empathy, improving communication, and creating a more inclusive workplace. That's why we teamed up with Flouria, providing you with quick access to a broad range of women's health professionals.

  • Daily lunches, snacks & drinks are provided at our office locations.

  • Next to fun events year-round, we throw notorious Christmas parties and organise an amazing yearly trip abroad with all employees.

  • Other perks include flexible working hours, full travel compensation and the working gear of your choice.

Interested in making an impact?

We would love to have a conversation with you!

Apply now, send us your CV and explain in your motivation letter why you’re excited about joining Fastned.

Here’s the next steps of the hiring process:

  • Screening call with Recruiter

  • Codility assignment and technical interview with our Engineers

  • Culture-fit conversation with the team

  • Closing Coffee Chat with our Head of Engineering / Director of Product & Engineering


Then, it’s time to welcome you on board to Fastned!


Fastned stands for equity and inclusion. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, gender identities, sexual orientations, religions, neurodiversity, disabilities, parental status or any other protected characteristic that makes you unique.

If you have questions or need further information regarding your application, please contact our recruitment team via fastned.nl

jobs.description:
About us

Tebi is building a modern connected hospitality operating system that helps entrepreneurs run their business more intelligently and smoothly. In one seamless platform, Tebi embeds sales, reservations, kitchen, inventory, and payments (as well as all the data that powers it) helping to automate work, streamline operations, and give hospitality owners the clarity and time they need to focus on what matters the most: creating great guest experiences.

Founded by Arnout Schuijff, co-founder of Adyen, and backed by €50 million in funding from Index Ventures & CapitalG, Tebi is build in service of hospitality first. Thousands of restaurants, cafés, bars, and coffee shops across the Netherlands, UK, Spain, Italy, Denmark, Germany, Finland, and Ireland.

About the role

As the Senior Product Manager on our AI team, you'll own how AI shows up in Tebi, from an AI agent embedded in the product to the AI capabilities that run through the platform. Tebi sits on a unified foundation of sales, payments, reservations, kitchen and inventory data, which gives our AI something most restaurant software can't offer: the full picture. You'll own the vision, strategy and roadmap, and turn that data into agents and features that save merchants time, cut costs and help them make better decisions on a busy service.

What you’ll do:

  • Define and own the vision and roadmap for Tebi's AI agent and AI capabilities across the product.

  • Work with AI engineers and data teams to ship agentic features that take real actions for merchants, not just answer questions.

  • Spend time with restaurant owners, managers and staff, plus Sales and Customer Success, to find the jobs where AI genuinely removes friction in their day.

  • Define how we measure quality and trust in AI features, including evals, accuracy, adoption and merchant outcomes, and use that to iterate quickly.

  • Decide where AI belongs in the product and where it doesn't, including guardrails, human-in-the-loop moments and when the merchant makes the final call.

  • Partner with all the other product teams so AI feels native to Tebi rather than bolted on.

What you'll need:

  • 8+ years of product management experience at a fast-growing tech company, with a track record of shipping impactful launches.

  • You are highly collaborative, able to partner effectively across the organization and build trust with both technical and operational teams.

  • Hands-on experience building AI-powered products and a solid grasp of their strengths and limits.

  • A data-driven mindset: you combine quantitative signals and qualitative feedback, and you know how to evaluate non-deterministic products.

  • You care about the balance between craft, speed, and outcomes.

This probably isn't the role for you if you're happiest on a structured environment with clear directions. We are looking for someone to set the direction and the vision for this team.

People who succeed at Tebi are independent, curious and passionate about hospitality. If this speaks to you we can be the right fit. Learn more about how we work from our Recipe here: https://www.tebi.com/gb/careers.

Benefits:

  • Generous start-up equity

  • Competitive Salary

  • Lunch provided in the office

  • Team building events

  • Unlimited time off

What is Restaurant Software?
Restaurants and other merchants use various software systems such as Point of Sale (POS), Reservations, Kitchen Display Systems (KDS), Payments, Inventory, Staffing, and the list goes on. These systems all need to speak to each other which they frequently don't. It's a mess, and we are fixing it.

From buying a croissant at a cafe to having dinner with friends, it's a €4 Trillion+ global market and a critical part of everyday life in today's economy.

How We Use AI at Tebi
We use AI the way our merchants use Tebi, to cut out the friction and get to what matters faster. We believe in a world where AI increases quality, efficiency and speed.

At Tebi, AI isn't a policy or a checkbox, it's just part of how we work. It helps us write, analyse, build, and improve but doesn't make the last call. If there's a smarter way to do something, we want to find it.

jobs.title: Senior Cloud Engineer
jobs.description:
At Luscii, we're creating space for care by developing and improving digital healthcare applications that make a real difference in people's lives through several applications. From Luscii Thuismeten, which helps healthcare professionals monitor patients remotely, to OMRON Connect, connecting millions of people with their health data through OMRON devices, and other applications that expand the possibilities of digital healthcare.

Together with healthcare professionals and partners around the world, we're working towards a future where people receive the right care in the right place. As our Senior Cloud Engineer, you'll help shape and modernise the cloud infrastructure behind these applications, building a reliable, scalable and future-proof foundation for millions of users worldwide.

Our applications have different histories, architectures and technical challenges. OMRON Connect, for example, runs on an AWS backend serving several million monthly active users. Parts of its infrastructure still carry legacy, including manual processes, scattered knowledge, inconsistent observability and release processes that make changes slower and riskier than they should be.

We're working towards a more consistent engineering foundation across our applications. Think Infrastructure as Code, cloud-native and event-driven architecture where it adds value, safe continuous deployment and observability by default. We're bringing more senior engineering expertise in-house to turn that ambition into concrete technical decisions, shared standards and a roadmap our teams can own. And that's where you come in 😉

Your role

You will work across our engineering teams, helping shape the cloud infrastructure behind our digital healthcare applications. Your focus will be on making the right architectural decisions, modernising existing platforms and enabling teams to independently build, maintain and improve their systems.

This isn't a greenfield architecture exercise. You will be improving live healthcare platforms while balancing technical improvements with product delivery, security, regulatory requirements and the realities of working with stakeholders across different countries, including the Netherlands and Japan.

What you will be doing, among others:

  • Own and evolve the Cloud & Backend roadmap, translating the engineering vision into clear priorities, trade-offs and next steps.

  • Drive cross-team architecture decisions to a close, making sure decisions are transparent, documented and followed through.

  • Establish shared technical standards and guardrails that allow teams to work autonomously without creating unnecessary dependencies.

  • Work hands-on with engineers on AWS and Terraform, reviewing designs and pull requests and challenging technical choices where needed.

  • Coach and pair with engineers, helping knowledge spread across teams and supporting the growth of seniority and ownership.

  • Work with product owners, QA, engineering leadership and colleagues in Japan to balance technical direction with product, regulatory, security and cost considerations.

  • Help move the platform towards automated infrastructure, safer deployments and stronger observability without relying on a big-bang rewrite.

The responsibilities outlined above reflect how we currently envision this role. As we continue to grow and evolve, the scope and focus of the position may naturally change, influenced by your own ideas and insights. The way we work is built around the belief that everyone's input matters. If you see opportunities to improve the way we do things, or believe a process could be designed differently to achieve a better outcome, we encourage you to bring those ideas forward. Discuss them with your teammates, challenge the status quo, and help shape how we move forward together.

Why Luscii?

Read more about working at Luscii / OMRON and how we work as a team. Together, we are working on a mission to create space for care. Freedom, autonomy and ownership are of great importance in this. You are responsible for your own results and work according to the principles of Holacracy. Luscii is part of OMRON DH; together we built for the long term. To work on making healthcare better.

Most important benefits

  • Salary: An annual maximum remuneration of approximately € 85.000 gross per year is estimated for this position (based on 32 hours per week – that’s full-time at Luscii), depending on the interviews, your experience, background and knowledge.

  • Remote-first: Work from anywhere in The Netherlands. We stay connected through monthly in-person team days called Assemblii.

  • Flexible setup: Create your own ideal workspace. Whatever works best for you - we’ve got you covered here. We do work from Mondays to Thursdays, as 32 hours per week is fulltime.

The ideal candidate…

… probably doesn't exist, but if you can tick most of the checkboxes below, please apply! We are looking for someone who enjoys taking ownership of complex technical challenges, makes pragmatic engineering decisions, and is excited about helping others succeed along the way.

You know when to step up, when to involve colleagues and when to move forward decisively. Working independently does not mean working in isolation for you. You feel at ease being both a self-starter and a committed team player, contributing to shared goals while taking responsibility for your own domain. You value open communication, transparency, and mutual trust.

  • You have at least 5+ years of experience in cloud/backend engineering and multiple years of hands-on experience with AWS and Terraform (Infrastructure as Code).

  • You are comfortable reviewing designs and pull requests. Experience with serverless and event-driven architectures is very valuable. All combined with experience in serverless AWS, Node.js/TypeScript tech stacks.

  • You actively coach, pair, review and share knowledge, with a focus on building ownership and seniority across the teams around you.

  • You understand what matters: the importance of making pragmatic technical choices within clear security, compliance and regulatory boundaries.

  • You are open to working in a Holacratic organization and curious about our way of organizing work, roles, and responsibilities;

  • English is our primary language for all internal communication at Luscii, so you're fluent in that language.

Interested? Apply now!

Would you like more information? Feel free to contact our recruiter Björn Bogerd via

What does the recruitment process look like?

You'll shape how Dyflexis looks and feels everywhere and take the brand from consistent to unmistakable. You'll work closely with our Brand Designer, the Marketing team, and UX/UI colleagues. You bring creative ideas, design thinking and a strong eye for digital. You turn business goals into concepts, carry one strong idea through every touchpoint, and know how to win people over with your work.

jobs.description:
Möchtest du das tägliche Leben von Millionen von Unternehmern in Deutschland (und bald in Europa) beeinflussen? Suchst du nach einem Arbeitsumfeld, das Vertrauen, Proaktivität und Autonomie schätzt? Stimmen unsere Company Values mit deiner Vision überein? Dann ist Pennylane der richtige Ort für dich!

 

Unsere Vision

Wir wollen das beliebteste finanzielle Betriebssystem für KMU (kleine und mittlere Unternehmen) und Steuerberatungsgesellschaften werden.

Wir helfen Unternehmern, sich von zeitraubenden Aufgaben rund um Buchhaltung und Finanzen zu befreien, während wir ihnen gleichzeitig Zugang zu wichtigen Finanzinformationen verschaffen, um die besten Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen zu treffen.

 

Über uns

Pennylane ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs in Frankreich (und jetzt auch in Deutschland!).

In 5 Jahren unseres Bestehens haben wir Folgendes erreicht:

💻 Wir haben uns als bahnbrechende Buchhaltungs- und Finanzsoftware für kleine Unternehmen und ihre Buchhalter bekannt gemacht.

💰 Wir haben insgesamt 225 Millionen Euro eingesammelt, unter anderem von Sequoia, dem berühmten Fonds aus dem Silicon Valley, der früh in Unternehmen wie Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal und viele mehr investiert hat...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Wir sind von 7 Mitbegründern auf 900 zufriedene Pennylaner angewachsen: Wir gelten heute als einer der besten Arbeitsplätze in Frankreich (auch remote), mit einer Bewertung von 4,6/5 auf Glassdoor.

🌍 Wir haben ein internationales Umfeld mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten aufgebaut, mit einer starken Remote-freundlichen Kultur, in der 30 % der Mitarbeiter bereits aus allen Teilen Europas arbeiten.

🤝 Wir haben das Vertrauen Tausender von Kunden und Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaften gewonnen und hervorragende Bewertungen erhalten.

🚀 Bereits mehr als 1 300.000 KMU (kleine und mittlere Unternehmen) und über 5000 Wirtschaftsprüfungsgesellschaften nutzen Pennylane in Frankreich!

Du willst als Account Executive Steuerkanzleien im Raum Düsseldorf oder München für eine neue Art der Zusammenarbeit mit ihren Mandanten gewinnen – am Telefon, per Video und vor Ort in der Kanzlei? Als eine:r der ersten Account Executives für unser deutsches Kanzleisegment baust du dir dein eigenes Gebiet auf, verantwortest den gesamten Vertriebszyklus bis zum Onboarding und entwickelst gemeinsam mit unserem Firms-Team den Vertriebsansatz für den deutschen Markt – mit dem Rückenwind eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs Europas.

Unsere Vision

Wir wollen das beliebteste finanzielle Betriebssystem für KMU (kleine und mittlere Unternehmen) und Steuerkanzleien werden.

Wir helfen Unternehmern, sich von zeitraubenden Aufgaben rund um Buchhaltung und Finanzen zu befreien, während wir ihnen gleichzeitig Zugang zu wichtigen Finanzinformationen verschaffen, um die besten Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen zu treffen. Steuerkanzleien geben wir die Plattform, mit der sie ihre Mandate effizienter betreuen und ihre Steuerberatung digital weiterentwickeln.

Über uns

Pennylane ist eines der am schnellsten wachsenden Fintechs Europas – seit 2025 auch in Deutschland. Das haben wir seit der Gründung 2020 erreicht:

💻 Wir haben uns als All-in-One-Plattform für Buchhaltung, Finanzen und die Zusammenarbeit zwischen Unternehmen und ihren Steuerberater:innen etabliert – KI-gestützt, cloudbasiert, mit offenen Schnittstellen.

💰 Wir haben rund 360 Millionen Euro Kapital eingesammelt – zuletzt 175 Millionen Euro in unserer Series E im Januar 2026, angeführt von TCV und Blackstone Growth, neben Investoren wie Sequoia, CapitalG (Alphabet) und DST Global. Unsere Bewertung liegt bei 3,5 Milliarden Euro.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Wir sind von 7 Mitbegründern auf über 900 Pennylaner:innen angewachsen, davon mehr als 400 in Tech, Data und Product – mit einer Bewertung von 4,6/5 auf Glassdoor.

🚀 Bereits mehr als 900.000 KMU und über 5.000 Steuerkanzleien nutzen Pennylane in Frankreich – in diesem Segment sind wir dort in fünf Jahren zum Marktführer geworden.

🇩🇪 Deutschland ist unser wichtigster Wachstumsmarkt: Geführt von Managing Director Tobias Janiesch wächst das deutsche Team in Berlin und München 2026 auf rund 100 Kolleg:innen. Du kommst in der Gründungsphase dazu und prägst, wie Pennylane hier verkauft.

Deine Mission

Du wirst eine:r der ersten Account Executives (m/w/d) – Steuerkanzleien in Deutschland sein. Deine Mission ist es, Steuerkanzleien in deiner Region für Pennylane zu gewinnen – du baust dir deine Pipeline selbst auf, überzeugst Kanzleiinhaber:innen in der Demo und vor Ort und begleitest deine Kanzleien vom Abschluss bis zum erfolgreichen Onboarding.

In Frankreich ist Pennylane in diesem Segment innerhalb von fünf Jahren zum Marktführer geworden. Du arbeitest mit dem bewährten Playbook und passt es gemeinsam mit unserem Sales Firms Director, an den du zunächst direkt berichtest, an den deutschen Kanzleimarkt an – als eine:r der Ersten gestaltest du mit, wie Pennylane hier an Kanzleien verkauft. Unser Prozess: Erstgespräch, Interview mit dem Sales Firms Director, Case Study, Abschlussgespräch mit Tobias Janiesch, Managing Director Deutschland.

Dein Team

Full-Cycle Sales: Du verantwortest den gesamten Prozess – von der Qualifizierung über die Produkt-Demo und den Abschluss bis zum Onboarding und Account Management deiner Kanzleien.

Outbound ist Kern: Rund 50 % deiner Pipeline baust du selbst auf – per Telefon, LinkedIn, Branchenevents und Kanzleibesuche. Ergänzt wird das durch Inbound-Leads und Empfehlungen. Wer nur auf Inbound wartet, wird hier nicht glücklich; wer gern aktiv Türen öffnet, umso mehr.

Starkes Setup: Dabei bist du nicht allein: Unser eigenes Customer-Success-Team in Berlin unterstützt dich bei Onboarding und Betreuung deiner Kanzleien, damit du genug Zeit für die Neukundengewinnung hast.

Regional organisiert: Du betreust eine feste Region – Düsseldorf/Nordrhein-Westfalen oder München/Bayern – per Inside Sales und vor Ort in den Kanzleien. Deshalb suchen wir dich dort, wo deine Kanzleien sind.

Im Aufbau: Du kommst zu einem kleinen Team von Account Executives dazu, das mit dir wächst – bald unter der Führung eines Team Leads Sales Firms in Berlin.

Beratender Vertrieb: Du gewinnst Kanzleiinhaber:innen und Partner:innen für eine neue Art der Zusammenarbeit mit ihren Mandanten. Du machst den Nutzen von Pennylane für den Kanzleialltag konkret und schaffst Vertrauen in die Einführung einer neuen Plattform.

Remote in deiner Region: Du arbeitest aus dem Homeoffice oder Coworking in deiner Region und bist regelmäßig bei Kanzleien vor Ort, auf Messen und bei Verbandsveranstaltungen. Etwa einmal im Monat kommst du für Team-Treffen in unser Berliner Office.

Du wirst für den Erfolg deiner Region verantwortlich sein durch:

  • Du verantwortest den MRR aus Steuerkanzleien in deiner Region und trägst zur Marktdurchdringung von Pennylane im deutschen Kanzleisegment bei.

  • Du baust eine systematische Outbound-Akquise für Kanzleien auf – Zielkundenlisten, Sequenzen, Events, Vor-Ort-Besuche – und hältst deine Aktivitätsquoten hoch.

  • Du führst Bedarfsanalysen und Produktdemos durch und begleitest komplexe Entscheidungsprozesse mit mehreren Stakeholdern bis zum Abschluss.

  • Du sorgst gemeinsam mit Customer Success für eine reibungslose Übergabe und baust deine Kanzleien aus, indem du die Anzahl der über Pennylane betreuten Mandanten steigerst.

  • Du dokumentierst deine Pipeline sauber im CRM und nutzt Pipeline- und Conversion-Daten, um dich selbst zu steuern.

Als Account Executive – Steuerkanzleien sind deine Ziele vielfältig:

  • Du erreichst deine Vertriebsziele und hast nach 3 Monaten eine qualifizierte Pipeline, nach 6 Monaten deine ersten Kanzleien und erste Referenzen.

  • Du baust ein Netzwerk von Botschafter-Kanzleien auf, die Pennylane weiterempfehlen.

  • Du vertrittst Pennylane auf Branchenevents, Fachmessen und Veranstaltungen von Steuerberaterverbänden in deiner Region.

  • Du bringst deine Markteinblicke in Product, Marketing und das SME-Sales-Team ein.

  • Du teilst deine Learnings und baust das Playbook für die nächsten AEs mit auf.

Dein Profil

  • Du bringst mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Vertrieb mit – mit komplexen, erklärungsbedürftigen Produkten, mehrstufigen Deal-Zyklen und mehreren Stakeholdern – und hast nachweislich Abschlüsse erzielt, die du selbst angebahnt hast.

  • Ein Plus: Du kennst den Markt der Steuerkanzleien oder das Accounting-/Fintech-Ökosystem – oder hast an Steuerberater:innen, Kanzleien oder andere Berufsträger verkauft. Wenn nicht, bringst du die Neugier mit, dich schnell einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast selbst Outbound gemacht: Kaltakquise bei Inhaber:innen und Entscheider:innen schreckt dich nicht – sie ist dein Hebel.

  • Du bist ein Builder: Du hast schon einmal ein Gebiet, einen Markt oder einen Prozess aufgebaut – idealerweise in einem schnell wachsenden Umfeld (Start-up oder Scale-up) – und baust Vertrauen auf, bei Kanzleiinhaber:innen wie im Team.

  • Du bist gern draußen: Field Sales ist für dich kein Kompromiss, sondern der Grund, warum du diesen Job willst – Kanzleibesuche, Messen und Verbandstermine gehören für dich dazu.

  • Du bist offen für Selbstreflexion und fühlst dich wohl dabei, Feedback zu geben und zu empfangen.

  • Du arbeitest bereichsübergreifend mit anderen Abteilungen zusammen – Marketing, Customer Success, Product und dem französischen HQ.

  • Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau (C2) – deine Kund:innen sind deutsche Kanzleien – und gutes Englisch für die Zusammenarbeit mit Paris.

  • Du lebst im Raum Düsseldorf oder München, hast einen Führerschein und eine gültige Arbeitserlaubnis für Deutschland – und bist gern bei Kunden vor Ort.

Was wir tun, um dein Arbeitsleben besser zu machen

🏡 Remote in deiner Region: Du arbeitest aus dem Homeoffice oder Coworking – mit monatlicher Coworking-Pauschale und einem Budget, um dein Zuhause in einen komfortableren Arbeitsplatz zu verwandeln.
